headline: Migration is a survival strategy—animals travel thousands of miles following food, warmth, or breeding grounds
universal_truth: Sometimes the best solution is to move; staying put isn't always the answer
fun_facts: Arctic terns migrate from pole to pole—44,000 miles per year, seeing two summers
Monarch butterflies travel 3,000 miles to a forest in Mexico they've never seen
Salmon return to the exact stream where they were born, navigating by Earth's magnetic field and smell
discussion_questions: How do animals know where to migrate without maps?
What would happen if migrating animals couldn't complete their journeys?
When in life is moving the best solution?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every year, billions of animals travel thousands of miles—birds flying pole to pole, whales crossing oceans, butterflies navigating to forests they've never seen. Migration is one of nature's most ambitious survival strategies.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Migration is dangerous and exhausting. Many animals die along the way. Why do so many species risk everything to travel so far instead of staying where they are?

options.text: To follow food supplies, reach breeding grounds, or escape harsh weather—staying would mean death
options.response: Yes. When conditions change, staying isn't an option. Migration trades the risks of travel for the certainty of death by staying. Movement is survival.

options.text: Animals migrate to explore new territories
options.response: Exploration isn't the goal—survival is. Animals return to the same places, not seek new ones...

q1.title: Following Food
q1.script: When winter kills plants in the north, herbivores must move south or starve. Predators follow prey. Whales follow plankton blooms across oceans. Migration tracks resources—animals move where the food is.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Following Food"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Built-In GPS
q2.script: How do animals navigate? Salmon smell their home stream. Birds sense Earth's magnetic field. Monarchs inherit a map they've never seen. Evolution built navigation systems into migrating animals—internal compasses pointing home.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Generational Journeys
q3.script: Some migrations span generations. Monarch butterflies take 4-5 generations to complete the round trip—no individual makes the whole journey. The knowledge passes down genetically. Great-great-grandchildren finish what ancestors started.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Sometimes the best solution is to move. Migration teaches that staying put isn't always the answer. When conditions change, the courage to travel may be what survival requires.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 153. Tomorrow, we'll explore shaping three dimensions—sculpture. Until then, consider: is there a migration you need to make?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Life Migration - When to Move
growTrack.activity: Have you made migrations in your life—moving for opportunity, escaping difficult situations, following resources? What made you move? What migrations might your future require? Sometimes staying is the risk, and moving is survival.
